papers.title: Assessing Reproducibility of Hi-C Chromatin Interactions using Stratum-Adjusted Irreproducible Discovery Rate
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Hi-C is a powerful technology for mapping chromatin interactions genome-wide. However, interaction loops identified from Hi-C contact maps often vary across replicate experiments due to experimental noise, making reproducibility assessment essential. A major challenge lies in the genomic distance dependence of interaction strength, which systematically affects reproducibility but is overlooked by existing methods for reproducibility assessment. Results We introduce Stratum-Adjusted Irreproducible Discovery Rate (SIDR), a novel statistical model that integrates distance stratification into the widely-used Irreproducible Discovery Rate (IDR) framework. SIDR explicitly models the confounding effect of genomic distance, enabling global control of irreproducibility across interaction ranges. Through simulations and real Hi-C datasets, we demonstrate that SIDR improves discriminative power and recovers more biologically meaningful interactions than existing approaches, making it a valuable tool for robust and reproducible Hi-C analysis. Availability The R package SIDR is freely available on GitHub https://github.com/qunhualilab/SIDR

papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要与动机**  
Hi-C是一种能够全面检测基因组范围内染色质相互作用的高效技术。然而，通过Hi-C接触图谱识别出的相互作用结构在重复实验中往往会因实验噪声而出现差异，因此对实验结果的可重复性进行评估至关重要。当前的可重复性评估方法普遍忽略了相互作用强度与基因组距离之间的依赖关系——这一因素会显著影响实验结果的可重复性，但现有方法并未对此予以充分考虑。  

**研究结果**  
我们提出了“分层调整型不可重复性检测率”（SIDR）这一新型统计模型。该模型将基因组距离对相互作用的影响纳入到广泛应用的“不可重复性检测率”分析框架中，从而能够系统地控制不同距离范围内实验结果的可重复性问题。通过模拟实验及真实的Hi-C数据集验证，我们发现SIDR在区分不同类型相互作用方面具有更强的能力，并且能比现有方法识别出更多具有生物学意义的相互作用结构。因此，它为进行可靠、可重复的Hi-C数据分析提供了有力工具。  

**软件可用性**  
SIDR R包已免费发布在GitHub上：https://github.com/qunhualilab/SIDR

papers.title: A data-driven evaluation of Optimization techniques in Cell Culture Media
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Optimizing cell-culture media for cultivated meat and cellular agriculture is both experimentally demanding and expensive. Traditional approaches employ Design of Experiments (DOE) to iterate through candidate formulations until a satisfactory medium emerges. Data-driven methods, and in particular Bayesian optimization (BO), can reach higher objective function values (here, titer) with fewer evaluations than classical DOE. Prior comparisons of optimizers on cell-media data have, however, relied largely on computational simulations rather than measured formulations, leaving researchers without evidence-based guidance on which strategy to adopt. Results We introduce two complementary benchmark protocols and apply them to six published cell-culture datasets. In the “Hide-the-Label” protocol each optimizer begins with only a partial view of the data and sequentially reveals hidden formulations, singly or in batches, reproducing the stepwise acquisition of costly laboratory measurements; the “Open Race” instead measures search efficiency of a method under a fixed evaluation budget. Both protocols were run across four generative surrogate classes (Gaussian process (GP), random forest, neural network, and Bayesian neural network), two difficulty regimes, and batch sizes of one to 20. GP-based BO was consistently the most sample-efficient strategy, locating hidden targets in substantially fewer evaluations than classical DOE designs or random search; its advantage narrowed but remained under injected noise and multi-modality, and optimizers built on more complex surrogates (deeper networks or adaptive ensembles) performed worse rather than better on these harder landscapes. We detail the mathematical basis of the benchmark, criteria for selecting suitable datasets, and how to obtain statistically robust conclusions in the presence of measurement bias and heterogeneity, and we provide a roadmap for selecting an optimization strategy in practice. Availability and Implementation Source code and the benchmark datasets are freely available at https://github.com/Amii-Applied-AI/amii-cell-ag-tools/tree/main/active-learning-for-cell-media and archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21501659

papers.llm_research_question_zh: 动机：优化用于培养肉及细胞农业的细胞培养基既需要大量的实验工作，又耗费高昂的成本。
llm_highlights_zh: 传统方法采用实验设计来反复测试各种候选配方，直到找到一种令人满意的方案为止。
数据驱动的方法，尤其是贝叶斯优化算法，能够在比传统设计实验方法更少的评估次数下，获得更高的目标函数值（在本例中即为抗体滴度）。
然而，以往针对细胞培养数据进行的优化器比较研究主要依赖于计算模拟结果，而非实际测量数据，因此研究人员在选择何种优化策略时缺乏基于实证的依据。
papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要**  
优化用于培养肉及细胞农业的细胞培养基既需要大量的实验工作，也耗费高昂的成本。传统方法通过实验设计来反复测试不同的配方，直至找到理想的培养基组成。而基于数据驱动的方法，尤其是贝叶斯优化算法，能够在较少的评估次数下获得更高的目标函数值（例如产物的滴度）。然而，以往针对细胞培养基优化的研究大多依赖于计算模拟结果，而非实际测量的数据，这使得研究人员在选择优化策略时缺乏依据。  

**研究方法**  
我们设计了两种互补的基准测试方案，并将其应用于六组已公开发布的细胞培养基数据集。在“隐藏标签”测试方案中，每种优化算法最初只能获取部分数据信息，随后会逐步揭示被隐藏的配方信息，这一过程模拟了实际实验中耗时且成本高昂的数据采集流程；而在“公开竞赛”测试方案中，则在固定的评估预算下比较各种算法的搜索效率。这两种测试方案均针对四种不同的生成模型（高斯过程、随机森林、神经网络及贝叶斯神经网络）、两种不同的难度等级，以及从1到20不等的批量处理规模进行了验证。  

**实验结果**  
基于高斯过程的贝叶斯优化算法在样本利用效率方面始终表现最佳——它在较少的评估次数内就能找到目标配方，其优势在存在噪声或数据具有多模态特征的情况下依然显著；而那些基于更复杂模型的优化算法在这些更具挑战性的环境中反而表现较差。我们详细阐述了这些基准测试的数学基础、选择合适数据集的标准，以及如何在测量偏差和数据异质性存在的情况下获得可靠的实验结果，并为实际应用中选择优化策略提供了指导方案。  

**代码与数据资源**  
相关源代码及基准测试数据集可免费获取，链接如下：  
https://github.com/Amii-Applied-AI/amii-cell-ag-tools/tree/main/active-learning-for-cell-media  
数据集的存档地址为：  
https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21501659

Traditional approaches employ Design of Experiments (DOE) to iterate through candidate formulations until a satisfactory medium emerges. Data-driven methods, and in particular Bayesian optimization (BO), can reach higher objective function values (here, titer) with fewer evaluations than classical DOE. Prior comparisons of optimizers on cell-media data have, however, relied largely on computational simulations rather than measured formulations, leaving researchers without evidence-based guidance on which strategy to adopt.

RESULTS: We introduce two complementary benchmark protocols and apply them to six published cell-culture datasets. In the "Hide-the-Label" protocol each optimizer begins with only a partial view of the data and sequentially reveals hidden formulations, singly or in batches, reproducing the stepwise acquisition of costly laboratory measurements; the "Open Race" instead measures search efficiency of a method under a fixed evaluation budget. all_papers.title: Assessing Reproducibility of Hi-C Chromatin Interactions using Stratum-Adjusted Irreproducible Discovery Rate
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Hi-C is a powerful technology for mapping chromatin interactions genome-wide. However, interaction loops identified from Hi-C contact maps often vary across replicate experiments due to experimental noise, making reproducibility assessment essential. A major challenge lies in the genomic distance dependence of interaction strength, which systematically affects reproducibility but is overlooked by existing methods for reproducibility assessment. Results We introduce Stratum-Adjusted Irreproducible Discovery Rate (SIDR), a novel statistical model that integrates distance stratification into the widely-used Irreproducible Discovery Rate (IDR) framework. SIDR explicitly models the confounding effect of genomic distance, enabling global control of irreproducibility across interaction ranges. Through simulations and real Hi-C datasets, we demonstrate that SIDR improves discriminative power and recovers more biologically meaningful interactions than existing approaches, making it a valuable tool for robust and reproducible Hi-C analysis. Availability The R package SIDR is freely available on GitHub https://github.com/qunhualilab/SIDR
all_papers.abstract:
MOTIVATION: Hi-C is a powerful technology for mapping chromatin interactions genome-wide. However, interaction loops identified from Hi-C contact maps often vary across replicate experiments due to experimental noise, making reproducibility assessment essential. A major challenge lies in the genomic distance dependence of interaction strength, which systematically affects reproducibility but is overlooked by existing methods for reproducibility assessment.

RESULTS: We introduce Stratum-Adjusted Irreproducible Discovery Rate (SIDR), a novel statistical model that integrates distance stratification into the widely-used Irreproducible Discovery Rate (IDR) framework. SIDR explicitly models the confounding effect of genomic distance, enabling global control of irreproducibility across interaction ranges. Through simulations and real Hi-C datasets, we demonstrate that SIDR improves discriminative power and recovers more biologically meaningful interactions than existing approaches, making it a valuable tool for robust and reproducible Hi-C analysis.

all_papers.llm_research_question_zh: 动机：Hi-C是一种能够在全基因组范围内检测染色质相互作用的高效技术。

一个主要挑战在于，相互作用强度与基因组序列之间的距离存在依赖性，这种依赖性会系统性地影响实验结果的可重复性，但现有的可重复性评估方法却忽视了这一因素。

all_papers.llm_rss_summary_zh:
**摘要与动机**  
Hi-C是一种能够全面检测基因组范围内染色质相互作用的高效技术。然而，通过Hi-C接触图谱识别出的相互作用结构在重复实验中往往会因实验噪声而出现差异，因此对实验结果的可重复性进行评估至关重要。当前的可重复性评估方法普遍忽略了相互作用强度与基因组距离之间的依赖关系——这一因素会显著影响实验结果的可重复性，但现有方法并未对此予以充分考虑。  

**研究结果**  
我们提出了“分层调整型不可重复性检测率”（SIDR）这一新型统计模型。该模型将基因组距离对相互作用的影响纳入到广泛应用的“不可重复性检测率”分析框架中，从而能够系统地控制不同距离范围内实验结果的可重复性问题。通过模拟实验及真实的Hi-C数据集验证，我们发现SIDR在区分不同类型相互作用方面具有更强的能力，并且能比现有方法识别出更多具有生物学意义的相互作用结构。因此，它为进行可靠、可重复的Hi-C数据分析提供了有力工具。  

**软件可用性**  
SIDR R包已免费发布在GitHub上：https://github.com/qunhualilab/SIDR

all_papers.primary_summary_raw: Hi-C is a powerful technology for mapping chromatin interactions genome-wide. However, interaction loops identified from Hi-C contact maps often vary across replicate experiments due to experimental noise, making reproducibility assessment essential. A major challenge lies in the genomic distance dependence of interaction strength, which systematically affects reproducibility but is overlooked by existing methods for reproducibility assessment. Results We introduce Stratum-Adjusted Irreproducible Discovery Rate (SIDR), a novel statistical model that integrates distance stratification into the widely-used Irreproducible Discovery Rate (IDR) framework. SIDR explicitly models the confounding effect of genomic distance, enabling global control of irreproducibility across interaction ranges. Through simulations and real Hi-C datasets, we demonstrate that SIDR improves discriminative power and recovers more biologically meaningful interactions than existing approaches, making it a valuable tool for robust and reproducible Hi-C analysis.
